_meta.source: Illustrative ERCOT capacity evolution 2026–2050. Based on model assumptions: coal retirements, gas-CC stable, renewable growth (wind 25→65 GW, solar 20→80 GW), storage 5→35 GW.
_meta.description: 25-year capacity trajectory by fuel type (GW). Shows: coal decline, gas-CC plateau, rapid wind/solar growth, storage entry starting ~2028, hydrogen/CCS/geothermal emerge post-2035.

narrative.coal: Retires from 18 GW (2026) to near-zero by 2050. Economic retirement threshold: ~1 yr FCO hurdle when inframarginal margin < 0.
narrative.gas_cc: Remains stable ~30 GW. Replacement of retired units occurs post-2035 as baseload needs shift to long-duration storage and hydrogen.
narrative.wind: Grows from 25 GW to 65 GW. Driven by low LCOE (~$25/MWh) and high-altitude resource availability.
narrative.solar: Grows from 20 GW to 80 GW. Lowest-cost resource. Capacity value (ELCC) declines with penetration but remains economically attractive.
narrative.storage: Grows from 5 GW (nominal) to 35 GW. Driven by arbitrage value (net of cycling loss) + capacity-value stack.
narrative.hydrogen: Entry post-2030. Enabled by low-carbon electricity; economics sensitive to carbon price path and electrolyzer CAPEX learning.
narrative.ccs: Entry ~2029. Gas-CC retrofit when simple payback < remaining life; capped at 3 GW/yr/ISO.
narrative.offshore_wind: Entry post-2030. Higher cost (~$50/MWh) but strong capacity factor (~45%) supports marginal entry after onshore saturation.
